newsitem.title: USA: NGPL limits natgas line deliveries Thurs.
newsitem.headline: NGPL limits natgas line deliveries Thurs.

text.p: Natural Gas Pipeline (NGPL) declared "critical time" on its Texas-Illinois pipeline for Thursday, limiting gas deliveries along the system due to bitter cold in the Midwest, the company said Wednesday.
NGPL's system runs via two main lines from western Texas, terminating in Illinois.
Temperatures across the middle of the country have plunged to well below the seasonal norm and more bitter cold weather is forecast in the Chicago area for Thursday into the weekend.

"To prevent potentially serious operational problems, (NGPL) is advising all shipper to ensure by communication with their operators that volumes equal to their nominations are being delivered into (NGPL's) system at receipt points," the company said in a statement.
The move is designed to ensure that users are not drawing more gas from the system than they have already agreed, or "nominated", in order to avoid shortages.
NGPL also said they are limiting hourly "takes" or delivieries from 0600-1200 CST, beginning Friday, to 120 percent of confirmed daily nominations.
Two segments, number 27 on the Gulf Coast and number 12 on the Amarillo system, were exempted from the hourly limits.
Withdrawals from the system exceeding nominated volumes will incur a penalty, NGPL said.
Volumes affected by the limitations were not disclosed.

"Critical time" or a "critical day" is typically declared by pipeline operators during periods of extreme cold to ensure customers buying firm transmission receive their gas and to avoid operational problems along the pipeline system.
NGPL is a subsidiary of Occidental Petroleum.
